content:
Hi all, I've been using Lean to formally verify safety properties of a Python LLM orchestration harness and thought this community might find it interesting.

The spec models the orchestrator as a state machine and proves 5 well-formedness invariants (token accounting, budget safety, checkpoint monotonicity, step bound, termination consistency) across all execution paths, 15 theorems total, no sorry.

The interesting part: I then used the spec as a guide for mutation testing. Negating each invariant conjunct produced mutations that expose gaps in both the test suite and the spec itself. One mutation (+= to = in cost accumulation) passes all 65 tests and the Lean spec, revealing a missing cost-monotonicity conjunct.

Code + proofs: https://github.com/Samsssd/formally-verified-llm-orchestration

Happy to hear any feedback on the proof style or spec design, I'm relatively new to Lean 4.
This topic was moved here from #general > formal verification of LLM orchestration invariants by Michael Rothgang.
